clue.text: Left out of rankings? Worried moves

indicators.note: taking something out of a word removes it, here the letter for left from the rankings word

parts.note: rankings in a race or contest are placings

explanation.surface: A question about someone dropped from a league table, followed by a comment on nervous manoeuvres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes L from PLACINGS. The definition describes the anxious walking to and fro of a worried person.
explanation.definitionFit: Pacing up and down is the restless back-and-forth walking of an anxious person, so these are the movements of worry.

clue.text: Excitement losing energy if I start to create calm

annotationWithheld.why: Excitement losing energy if I start to create calm (7): the wordplay needs PAC + IF I + C, i.e. PACE losing E, but 'Excitement' does not mean pace; no blog or reprint found to show the printed word is misread
annotationWithheld.clue: Excitement losing energy if I start to create calm

clue.text: Designer's deliveryman catching you in Paris

definitions.note: possessive here reads as 'designer is', so the definition is just the designer

indicators.note: the deliveryman word catches, i.e. holds inside it, the French for you

parts.note: a courier is someone who delivers packages
tu is the familiar French word for you

explanation.surface: A fashion designer's messenger is spotted carrying something in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' puts TU inside COURIER. Read 'Designer's' as 'Designer is' for the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A couturier is a fashion designer who makes high-end bespoke clothes.

clue.text: Being in the dark when everyone else is in the dark?

definitions.text: Being in the dark when everyone else is in the dark?

parts.words: Being in the dark when everyone else is in the dark?
parts.note: the first 'in the dark' means unable to see, the second means at ...-time, describing a sight condition that only bites after sunset

explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on two senses of 'in the dark': unable to see, and literally in darkness after sunset.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical condition is an inability to see in poor light, so the sufferer cannot see when others are merely in darkness.

clue.text: African region said NZ law needs reforming

indicators.note: a law that needs reforming must be reshaped, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone reports that a New Zealand statute needs to be changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs reforming' rearranges SAIDNZLAW. NZ looks like an abbreviation to expand, but it is just two letters of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This southern African kingdom, now officially Eswatini, lies between South Africa and Mozambique.

clue.text: Cracking code's strange, but acceptable behaviour

indicators.note: cracking a code breaks it open, so the letters of the word code are rearranged

parts.note: rum is an old British word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Breaking a cipher seems odd but is perfectly proper conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking' rearranges CODE to DECO, then RUM follows. RUM meaning strange is dated British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorum is propriety, the polite and seemly conduct expected in company.

clue.text: Points to start from after discharging University obligations

indicators.note: discharging something lets it go, so the letter for university is released from the word

parts.note: debuts are first appearances, the points at which careers start

explanation.surface: Advice on where to begin once a graduate's university loans are cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharging' drops U from DEBUTS; 'after' is a link. The surface hints at paying off student loans, which is the definition's own field.
explanation.definitionFit: Debts are sums owed, financial obligations to be repaid.

clue.text: Garnish reconsidered as flavouring

indicators.note: to garnish a dish is to dress it up, so the letters of the following words are dressed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A garnish is rethought and pressed into service as a seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Garnish' rearranges RECONSIDEREDAS, all fourteen letters. It reads as a noun in the surface but works as an imperative verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The dried fruits of the coriander plant are a common spice used to flavour curries and pickles.

clue.text: Take hope? Not half — doctor's prescribing lozenge

parts.note: R abbreviates recipe, Latin for take, printed at the head of a prescription

indicators.note: only half of the word is used, its first two letters of four

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a British doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor tells a patient to take heart, at least partly, while writing out a cough sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' keeps HO of HOPE. R for 'take' is the prescription symbol; 'prescribing' is a link fitting the doctor scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhomb, or rhombus, is the diamond shape, which heraldry and geometry also call a lozenge.

clue.text: Make error in text-vague writer forgetting name

parts.note: misty means hazy or vague

indicators.note: a word that forgets something loses it, here the letter for name

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: Advice about getting something wrong in writing, linked to a hazy author who cannot recall a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgetting' drops N from PEN to leave PE. The printed 'test' is an OCR slip for 'text'.
explanation.definitionFit: To mistype is to hit the wrong key, introducing an error into typed words.

clue.text: Held on, first of climbers needing a breather

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the climbers word is taken

parts.note: a lung is an organ you breathe with

explanation.surface: A lead mountaineer, gasping for air, keeps a grip on the rock face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a breather' looks like a rest stop but means the organ that breathes.
explanation.definitionFit: Clung is the past tense of cling, to grip tightly or hold fast.

clue.text: Almost wake up after input of dull talker about trees

indicators.note: an input is something put in, so the bore word goes inside
almost all of the word is used, so its last letter goes

parts.note: to arouse someone is to wake them
a bore is a tedious person who talks too much

explanation.surface: Someone nearly stirs after a tedious speaker has droned on about forestry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts AROUSE to AROUS, and 'input of' puts BORE inside it; 'after' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Arboreous is a learned adjective meaning wooded or relating to trees, from the Latin for tree.

clue.text: Religious site -water source seen by wondrous baby in sea

parts.note: a fount is a spring or source of water

indicators.note: wondrous suggests something marvellously transformed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spring is spotted near a remarkable infant floating in the ocean at a holy place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wondrous' rearranges BABYINSEA to AINSABBEY; the 'in' is fodder, not a container. FOUNTAINS ABBEY is a ruined Cistercian monastery in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: This ruined abbey in North Yorkshire was one of England's largest Cistercian monasteries.

clue.text: See 11
Scale — Celsius-given support

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Celsius on a thermometer
a limb, such as a leg, holds up the body, and a tree's limb bears weight

explanation.surface: A temperature scale is given some backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scale' first looks like a measuring scale, prompted by Celsius, but it is the verb meaning to ascend.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale a wall or mountain is to go up it, to ascend.

clue.text: See 3 down
Where you'll find certain craft are moored at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of these words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A remark about boats tied up while out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges AREMOORED. The surface points to boats, but the craft are aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerodrome is a small airfield, the base for light aircraft.

clue.text: Near failing? Trail's becoming strong again

indicators.note: the word near is failing, falling apart, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a scent is the trail an animal leaves for hounds to follow

explanation.surface: A tracker, almost giving up, finds the trail picking up once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' rearranges NEAR to RENA, then SCENT follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Renascent means reviving or being reborn, regaining vigour after a decline.

clue.text: Hope a gran's involved — or will this beckon?

indicators.note: involved means tangled or intricate, so the letters of these words are mixed up

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter, so only the word gran is used

explanation.surface: Here's hoping a grandmother gets involved, otherwise a children's home awaits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges HOPEAGRAN. The definition carries on from the surface: without a gran to step in, a child may face this institution.
explanation.definitionFit: An orphanage is a home for children whose parents have died, so it awaits a child with no family to care for them.

clue.text: Most of class instructed? That's not allowed

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: a form is a school class in Britain
bidden means ordered or told to do something

explanation.surface: A question about a mostly obedient class, then a ruling that something is banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' cuts FORM to FOR. FORM for a school class is British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbidden means prohibited, banned by a rule or authority.

clue.text: Start game, following top player away

parts.note: an ace is a star performer
off means away, as in going off

explanation.surface: A match begins with the star player absent.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun phrase: the act that starts an ice hockey game.
explanation.definitionFit: In ice hockey a face-off begins play, with the puck dropped between two opposing players.

clue.text: Tearaway needs a little space to mature

parts.note: a rip is a reckless, dissolute person, much like a tearaway
an en is a printer's space half the width of an em

explanation.surface: An unruly youngster needs some room to grow up.
explanation.walkthrough: EN is a typesetting unit of space. 'to' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To ripen is to become ready or fully developed, as fruit does.

clue.text: Girl to fall ill — a result of holiday in sun, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things reversed, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: to ail is to become sick
a tan is the browned skin left by sunbathing

explanation.surface: A young woman thinks back on getting sick and on her suntan from a beach holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns AIL + A + TAN, giving NAT + A + LIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Natalia is a feminine given name, popular in Russia and Spain.

clue.text: Impregnable?

parts.note: read as unable to be made pregnant, unable to conceive a baby, rather than unconquerable

explanation.walkthrough: 'Impregnable' usually means unconquerable; the clue reads it as unable to be made pregnant. The real phrase describes packaging that small children cannot open.
explanation.definitionFit: Packaging built so that young children cannot open it is described this way, and the pun recasts it as resisting conception.

clue.text: Artist, no old man, put in tomb

indicators.note: no means without, so the father word is removed

parts.note: a painter is an artist
pa is an informal word for father, often called the old man

explanation.surface: A painter, fatherless, is laid in a grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes PA from PAINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury a body in a grave or vault.

clue.text: See 21
Stone from this river only looks precious

definitions.text: Stone from this river only looks precious

parts.words: Stone from this river only looks precious
parts.note: the costume-jewellery gem named after a German waterway is glittering paste, not a real gem

explanation.walkthrough: Rhinestones, imitation diamonds, take their name from the Rhine, where rock crystal was first collected for them.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhinestone, a paste imitation diamond, is named after this European river.

clue.text: See 6 down
Lateral thinking should — suggest place for clandestine affairs

definitions.text: Lateral thinking should — suggest place for clandestine affairs

parts.words: Lateral thinking should — suggest place for clandestine affairs
parts.note: lateral means at the side, and thinking that way points to where secret liaisons are said to be conducted, aside from a marriage

explanation.walkthrough: Lateral literally means at the side; a secret affair is one conducted away from the main relationship, in a spatial phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means sideways in position and also describes secret romances outside a marriage.

clue.text: Weak backing about one modern form of communication

indicators.note: the reversed weak word goes about, round, the numeral one
backing means going backwards, so the word for weak is read in reverse

parts.note: lame means feeble, as a lame excuse is
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Feeble support for a single newfangled way of keeping in touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns LAME to EMAL, and 'about' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic mail is a relatively recent means of sending messages between computers.

clue.text: Predict payment will secure sources of metal

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the payment word holds the ores inside it

parts.note: a fee is a payment for a service
ores are rocks from which metals are extracted

explanation.surface: A forecaster says the charge will lock in mining deposits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will secure' puts ORES inside FEE. 'sources of' looks like a first-letters signal but is part of the definition of ORES.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee is to see ahead, to know or forecast something before it happens.

clue.text: Group backing medicinal fluids as part of larger picture?

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the group word is read in reverse

parts.note: a set is a group of things
sera, the plural of serum, are fluids used in vaccines and antitoxins

explanation.surface: A party supports medicines as one element in the bigger scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns SET to TES. The question mark signals that the larger picture is literal: a mosaic.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one small tile of the many that make up a mosaic image.
